t: Integers With Multiple Sum of Two Cubes
o: Find all x <= n expressible as a^3 + b^3 (positive integers, a <= b) in at least two distinct ways — Taxicab-like numbers. Since n <= 1e9, cube roots reach 1000, so there are only ~500k pairs: enumerate them all and count.
k: cube_root(n) <= 1000, so brute-force pair enumeration is ~5*10^5 iterations.
Hash-map counting of pair sums, then filter counts >= 2 and sort.

a.i: For a = 1.. while 2a^3 <= n, for b = a.. while a^3+b^3 <= n, increment count[a^3+b^3]. Collect keys with count >= 2.
s: Double loop over (a, b) with the sum-bound pruning.
Count sums in a hash map.
a.t: O(cbrt(n)^2) ≈ 5*10^5 pair enumerations for n = 1e9, plus sorting the (few) results

w: The cube-root bound makes brute force viable; use 64-bit integers since cubes near 1e9 cubed overflow 32 bits. Pitfall: the outer loop bound 2a^3 <= n (since a <= b). Follow-up: exactly two representations (Hardy-Ramanujan numbers), or three representations.
